# Fixture provenance

- rings-grid.svg, rosette.svg, and petal-flower.svg are the 6 × 6 in
  (152.4 × 152.4 mm) photo tracings copied byte-for-byte from
  examples/gallery/. Their parametric source is
  examples/gallery/generate_tiles.py. Pete approved this fixture swap on
  2026-07-15 to resolve M7 without relaxing the bounded fuse-hop contract.
- illustrator-export.svg is an unmodified real Adobe Illustrator 29.8.2 SVG
  export found locally and used with its original complex structure intact.
- inkscape-export.svg is exported by the locally installed Inkscape binary from
  inkscape-source.svg.
- The remaining files are intentionally small, deterministic adversarial cases.
- stack-rosette-motif.svg is an authored four-petal continuous-path motif used
  only as the raised second tier in the F4.7 stack-job fixture.
- stack-job.toml combines the real photo-traced rings-grid base with that small
  motif in both calibrated and drape acceptance cases.
- stress-10000.svg is generated deterministically by scripts/generate_stress_fixture.py
  and committed so offline tests do not manufacture their own evidence.
- Weave-mode meshes under mesh/ are deterministic synthetic fixtures generated by
  scripts/generate_mesh_fixtures.py. Their dimensions and adversarial purpose are
  documented in mesh/README.md. They do not stand in for the real vessel exports,
  which are frozen separately under reference/ with hashes and GH provenance.
- mesh/teapot-lid.obj and mesh/tall-tumbler.obj were added on 2026-08-02 for the
  interior series (solid and infill). They are the same deterministic generator
  output as the rest of the family — a shallow lid to fill solid, a tall tumbler
  whose ribs must register through more than thirty layers — and are shaped for
  the house test slice settings (layer_height 2.0, sample_spacing 1.0,
  bead_width 5.0), not traced from any real pot.
- The >500,000-triangle Weave refusal case is deliberately not committed. The same
  generator writes a 500,001-face binary PLY into pytest's temporary directory so
  the true budget boundary is exercised without permanent repository waste.
- draw-fill/ holds small hand-written Draw drawings for area fills (added
  2026-10-01), written the way the Draw editor writes a pass: millimetre
  viewBox, y down, one root data-clayline-fill attribute. self-crossing.svg is
  one line crossing itself into a star with a loose tail, like Pete's drawing;
  self-crossing-bare.svg is the same line without the attribute, pinned against
  the G-code HEAD wrote before fills existed. The rest are one shape each
  (square, L, ring with a hole, round tile, dumbbell, pinched neck, an open
  shape, three small triangles) chosen for the rule its test pins. Added after
  the engine review the same day, each reproducing one of its findings: four
  Box squares (boxes.svg), a 100 x 40.04 mm box (near-multiple-box.svg), a
  box with a 24.24 mm arm (arm.svg), a tile with a ring off its middle
  (hole-off-centre.svg), a square with a line in from one side (spur.svg) or a
  loose line inside (loose-line.svg), the pinched neck in Straight rows
  (pinched-rows.svg), and turned-pass.svg, a self-crossing line the review's
  sweep script drew at random (seed 13), one of whose fills the finished slice
  cannot print over a pass turned 33 degrees. Added when a fill began running
  on into a line up to a coil and a half away: an equilateral triangle
  (triangle.svg), whose line starts on a 60-degree corner too far from its
  fill to run on from, and the square with a line in from its side 1 mm from
  the corner its line starts on (spur-by-corner.svg), which a run-on would
  cross.
- photo/solid-64x48.heic and photo/sideways-64x48-orientation6.heic are tiny
  synthetic HEIC samples (one flat colour, 64 × 48 pixels; the second tagged
  EXIF orientation 6) for the reference photo's HEIC fallback. They were
  encoded once on 2026-10-05 with pillow-heif 1.5.0 at quality 80 and committed,
  because the app now uses decode-only pi-heif and the tests cannot encode HEIC.
